question: Do retrieval-augmented clinical note classifiers keep their advantage over fine-tuned encoders when evaluated on a later admission year?

audience.who: Clinical NLP researchers choosing between retrieval augmentation and fine-tuning for coding tasks.

citations.citation: Example A et al. Retrieval for ICD coding.
Example B et al. Temporal drift in clinical NLP.

closest_prior_work.citation: Example A et al. Retrieval for ICD coding (2025).
closest_prior_work.what_it_shows: Retrieval helps on a random split of one admission period.
closest_prior_work.our_difference: Temporal split across admission years with a matched fine-tuned baseline.

decisive_analysis.description: Temporal-split macro-F1 of both model families on the later admission year.

primary_endpoint.metric: macro-F1 on the held-out later admission year
primary_endpoint.matched_baseline: fine-tuned encoder with the same label set and training years
primary_endpoint.split: train on earlier years, test on the latest year
primary_endpoint.decision_rule: retrieval model better by at least 1.0 macro-F1 with a bootstrap 95% CI excluding 0
primary_endpoint.stop_rule: stop if the CI includes 0 after the pre-registered run

computational_only_rationale: Re-analysis of an existing de-identified database; no new data collection, wet lab or human contact.

cost_estimate.basis: Reuses the clinical text pipeline from the asset index; one comparable campaign used about 10 GPU hours.

compute_plan.notes: Fine-tuning on the reserved container GPU; preprocessing and evaluation in the container.
